newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity eases through to Monday.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity eases through to Monday.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) eased Wednesday with some expectations of warmer weather through to at least Monday, brokers and marketers said.
Forecasts called for normal temperatures throughout Texas into Sunday, with some possible below-normal temperatures next week.
ERCOT firm, peak power for Friday delivery was assessed in the $29.00-31.00 range from next day delivery discussion on Tuesday of $30.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.

ERCOT peak power for Monday delivery was pegged at similar levels to those of Friday, with some traders planning to do business on Friday ahead of some possible cold weather early next week, the sources said.
Hourly power for Wednesday delivery was said to be trading at $37.00-39.00 per MWh.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power transactions were pegged steady at $16.00-18.00 for Friday business, the sources said.
ERCOT December peak power was notionally said to be talked steady at $31.00-33.00, while January/February peak power was steady at $31.50-32.00, the sources said.
